text:
deploy-bot: starting rollout: model=v3.1-hottokenizer, rollout_id=rl-9812, strategy=gradual-30%
Alex W: paging oncall — autoscaler alerts spiking in us-west-2, queue length up fast. Getting 504/502s from hosted endpoints.
Tilly (oncall): I'm on it. any customer-facing impact yet?
Maria G: yes, support reported ~6 customers seeing intermittent 502s and high TTFB. SLO errors rising in the last 10m.
Cheng O: looking at metrics — GPU occupancy jumped ~40% on pools serving the new variant. p50 latency up 2x and p99 is showing huge tail. KV-cache miss rate also rose.
Alex W: this was a tokenizer change + model packaging that increases per-token memory (more context indexes). Might be increasing KV pressure. Rollout started ~18m ago.
infra-bot: Alert: autoscaler_group=rg-gpu-usw2 hit max_replicas=48, queue_depth=4200, throttle_rate=20%.
Tilly (oncall): can we pause the rollout? Maria, can support gate the rollout flag?
Maria G: pausing canary now. deploy-bot: pause accepted for rollout rl-9812. Canary traffic frozen.
Cheng O: good. but queued requests keep piling on existing instances. Autoscaler can't add more due to pool quota cap — hitting cloud quota for GPUs in the region.
Alex W: immediate mitigations: 1) route new traffic to fallback model (v3.0-stable) which is already warm. 2) increase throttle for low-priority routes. 3) ask infra to request quota increase and enable short-term burst pool if possible.
Maria G: routing to fallback now — updating routing policy to prefer model v3.0-stable for production routes.
infra-bot: routing update applied. 62% of requests now rerouted to fallback model.
Customer Ops: notifying impacted customers that we are mitigating and we'll follow up. Template msg sent to those affected.
Cheng O: ran a quick heap profile — per-request KV metadata size increased by ~28% due to tokenizer token id expansion. That explains increase in KV cache size and more frequent eviction/warmups.
Tilly (oncall): any chance to reduce context length on the fly for the variant? like enforce a shorter max_context in the router?
Alex W: yes, we can enforce server-side truncation for v3.1-hottokenizer but since canary is paused and traffic is rerouted, priority is draining the queue. After we get headroom we'll either revert the model or ship a patched tokenizer build.
Maria G: queue drain plan: 1) increase per-instance concurrency for fallback model, 2) temporarily lower priority/timeouts for batch jobs, 3) drop extremely large requests > 16k tokens with a 400 response + friendly message.
Cheng O: implemented a rule to drop >16k token requests at the gateway. gateway logs: 
```
[drop-rule] request_id=*** size=19500 tokens reason=context-exceeds-safety
```
infra-bot: executed scaling request: requested_additional_replicas=12 to burst pool; cloud provider rejected due to quota. Ticket opened with cloud support (INC-2241).
Alex W: I'm going to open an emergency quota request and cc infra lead. Also actioning an immediate temporary capacity reallocation from non-critical pools.
Tilly (oncall): handoff — I'm going offline in 15m, if this is still active escalate to Cheng.
Tilly (oncall): @Cheng O you on for next shift?
Cheng O: yes, I can take the handoff. I'll keep the thread updated.
Maria G: support update template posted to status page and to customers: will include ETA for rollbacks.
Customer Ops: customers acknowledged and asked for ETA — replied "mitigation in progress, fallback routing applied, full remediation ETA 4-8 hours".
Alex W: post-mortem hypotheses: 1) Tokenizer change increased internal token space leading to larger KV keys and more cache pressure. 2) Model packaging changed attention cache indexing causing higher memory per sequence. Both cause higher per-request GPU memory and lower throughput.
Cheng O: next steps while draining: 1) keep canary paused, 2) gather perf profiles on v3.1 in staging with forced shorter context to reproduce, 3) prepare rollback artifact for v3.0 and test fast switch path, 4) request cloud quota bump and temporary burst pool.
infra-bot: note: manual pool reallocation started: migrating 2 GPUs from batch-nonprod to prod-burst. ETA 6m.
Maria G: re-run hitless switch to fallback model initiated. Monitoring tail latencies.
Alex W: monitoring shows queue dropping from 4200 -> 900 in 12m after routing change and drop-rule. p99 tail latency improving but still above SLO.
Tilly (oncall): leaving handoff notes for Cheng: check pool quotas, follow INC-2241 updates, coordinate with infra for GPU reassign, confirm rollback artifact readiness, and keep customers updated.
Cheng O: ack. I'll post timeline and final remediation plan once we confirm either a rollback or a patched tokenizer.
deploy-bot: rollback available: artifact=v3.0-stable@sha256:abcd1234 — requires 2m for switch.
Cheng O: initiating rollback to v3.0-stable for all production traffic in 2m to fully recover.
Alex W: after rollback completes we'll run a tighter preflight for any tokenizer/packaging change that touches KV schema and ramp more slowly. Add a perf-gate to the rollout playbook.
Customer Ops: customers notified about rollback and asked to validate behavior. No new incidents reported so far.
infra-bot: rollback completed. active_replicas now stable. queue_depth=120.
Cheng O: post-rollback metrics look good — p99 back to baseline, errors dropping. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then open a follow-up postmortem doc.
Maria G: thanks everyone. filing incident ticket INC-2026 with initial notes and action items.
Alex W: thanks team — great coordination. :thumbsup:
